reference.question: Calculate the value of \(\sin 30^\circ+\cos 60^\circ\).
reference.solution:
Method 1: Substitute special-angle values

\(\sin 30^\circ=1/2\) and \(\cos 60^\circ=1/2\). Their sum is 1.

nodes.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
nodes.label: 4.NF.B.3a

nodes.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model . Examples: 3/8 = 1/8 + 1/8 + 1/8 ; 3/8 = 1/8 + 2/8 ; 2 1/8 = 1 + 1 + 1/8 = 8/8 + 8/8 + 1/8.
nodes.label: 4.NF.B.3b

nodes.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
nodes.label: 4.NF.B.3d

nodes.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers. For example, determine the unknown number that makes the equation true in each of the equations 8 + ? = 11, 5 = ? – 3, 6 + 6 = ?.
nodes.label: 1.OA.D.8

nodes.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract.* Examples: If 8 + 3 = 11 is known, then 3 + 8 = 11 is also known. (Commutative property of addition.) To add 2 + 6 + 4, the second two numbers can be added to make a ten, so 2 + 6 + 4 = 2 + 10 = 12. (Associative property of addition.) *Students need not use formal terms for these properties.
nodes.label: 1.OA.B.3
